study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., The Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Benchmark and identify the optimal normative modeling approach for brain morphometric data by comparing algorithms and covariate choices, and quantify performance and stability across age and sample sizes.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (87 datasets; ENIGMA Lifespan WG and collaborators)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The manuscript states that data were collated from 87 datasets across multiple regions as part of ENIGMA Lifespan and related cohorts; these constitute the normative reference sample.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "We collated de-identified data from 87 datasets from Europe, Australia, the USA, South Africa, and east Asia ... Data use aligned with the policies of the ENIGMA Lifespan Working Group"

rci2_hc_n.reason: The abstract and results section clearly state the total sample size of healthy individuals used for model development.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: A total of 37 407 healthy individuals from 87 datasets from 20 countries were included in this study.

rci3_hc_age.answer: Phase: Uninvestigated | mean: 39.88 | sd: 23.47 | median: NR | iqr: NR | min: 3 | max: 90

rci4_hc_sex.reason: The Results section clearly states the sex distribution with exact counts. I calculated the percentages from the provided counts (19964/37407 = 53.4% and 17443/37407 = 46.6%).
rci4_hc_sex.supporting_text: This sample consisted of 19 964 females and 17 443 males.

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: Morphometric features were extracted from whole-brain T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: "Morphometric feature extraction from whole-brain T1-weighted images was implemented with the standard pipelines in the FreeSurfer image analysis suite ..."

nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: "We developed this framework with regional morphometric data from 37 407 healthy individuals ... The model and scripts described here are freely available through CentileBrain."

caa2_diseases_studied.reason: They explicitly state using psychosis as an example and use the HCP-EP cohort.
caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: "We tested whether normative brain regional Z-scores have an advantage ... using psychosis as an example ... Human Connectome Project-Early Psychosis Study (HCP-EP)."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: MFPR with non-linear age and global covariates outperformed alternatives; performance plateaued at ~3000 samples; Z-scores improved psychosis classification over observed measures and showed longitudinal stability.
